program.merge_policy: accumulate twenty 25-finding passes; consolidate, admit, validate, and merge once after Wave 2000

source_provenance: Sider Scholar + NCBI PubMed exact-source verification
repository-wide PMID collision screening against prior enrichment waves, including pending Waves 501-1000

policy.validation_strategy: PMID-level dedupe/source verification during authoring; expensive repository-wide validation only after Wave 2000

waves.focus: Randomized double-blind trial in 120 children with cerebral palsy and persistent sleep problems found melatonin improved diary-derived total sleep time and sleep-onset latency over 12 weeks with few reported adverse effects; pediatric neurologic-population findings should not be generalized to healthy children or adults.

Randomized double-masked crossover trial in 64 adults with advanced glaucoma found no significant melatonin-versus-placebo benefit for subjective or actigraphic sleep outcomes or vision-related quality of life despite within-time improvements in both groups; useful direct null sleep evidence in a visually impaired population.

Multicentre placebo-controlled trial in adults age 70 and older receiving systemic cancer treatment was stopped early for futility and found no significant global quality-of-life benefit from melatonin among compliant participants; supplementation appeared safe, but attrition and advanced-cancer context limit broader inference.

Meta-analysis of 28 randomized trials pooled heterogeneous dietary-supplement interventions and reported modest improvements in PSQI, sleep efficiency, total sleep time, latency and WASO, but cross-ingredient category pooling prevents attributing the effect to any one nutrient or product.

Eight-week RCT in 84 adults with poor sleep found no significant treatment-by-time effect on primary PSQI or ISI outcomes for heat-treated Limosilactobacillus fermentum PS150; exploratory biomarker and higher-insomnia-severity subgroup signals remain strain/formulation-specific and hypothesis-generating.

Small randomized double-blind study in 30 young women with primary dysmenorrhea found a chamomile-plus-L-theanine beverage improved several pain, mood and daytime-function measures versus baseline/control, but the multi-ingredient beverage and short exposure prevent attributing effects to either ingredient alone.

Translational study including an eight-week randomized human trial reported improved subjective sleep quality and sleep duration with a walnut-peptide plus theanine combination, alongside animal HPA/GABA findings; the human effect is combination-specific and cannot be assigned to theanine alone.

Twelve-week randomized placebo-controlled trial in 50 adults found a proprietary mushroom blend improved several anxiety, fatigue, depression and PSQI measures with changes in cortisol, ACTH and CRP; small sample and multicomponent proprietary formulation require a product-specific firewall.

Randomized double-blind trial in 48 third-molar surgery patients found a single preoperative sublingual melatonin dose did not improve perioperative anxiety, psychomotor performance, postoperative sleep or early post-traumatic-stress symptoms versus placebo; useful acute high-exposure null evidence.

Double-blind RCT in 109 medically hospitalized adults age 65 and older was stopped early for futility and found no significant benefit from short-course melatonin for delirium incidence, sleep duration, 28-day mortality or readmission.

Meta-analysis of 22 ICU randomized trials involving 3,706 patients found melatonin or melatonin-receptor-agonist strategies associated with lower delirium incidence, but no significant effect on delirium duration, ICU stay or mortality; intervention heterogeneity and mixed-agonist evidence constrain melatonin-only inference.

Nine-RCT meta-analysis involving 788 participants found melatonin improved several migraine-frequency, severity and sleep measures versus placebo, while active-comparator results favored amitriptyline on some efficacy endpoints; supports condition-specific adjunctive evidence, not general sleep or analgesic superiority.

Tiny randomized pilot in children under five with neurodevelopmental disorders comparing melatonin plus 5-HTP versus melatonin plus L-tryptophan found no significant between-group sleep differences; a within-group motor-activity signal in 5-HTP completers is hypothesis-generating amid high attrition.

Meta-analysis of three pediatric atopic-dermatitis RCTs found melatonin shortened sleep-onset latency and modestly lowered clinician-rated severity, but total sleep duration and IgE were not improved and the SCORAD change did not clearly exceed the minimal clinically important difference.

Three-arm randomized trial in adults age 50 to 85 with recurrent leg cramps found magnesium hydrochloride did not reduce cramp frequency versus placebo, while compression stockings did; direct null evidence against routine magnesium efficacy for this indication.

Systematic review and meta-analysis in menopausal women found suggestive femoral-neck bone-density benefit but no consistent improvements in sleep, menopausal symptoms, mood, sexual function, BMI or insulin; prevalent combination interventions and heterogeneity prevent isolating melatonin's independent effect.

Phase I/II adjunctive trial of very-high-dose melatonin with ocrelizumab in primary progressive multiple sclerosis was halted after grade 1 to 2 hypertransaminasemia in three participants; this is regimen-specific cross-therapy safety evidence, not a general low-dose melatonin risk estimate.

Meta-analysis of 10 chronic-kidney-disease RCTs found melatonin modestly increased HDL, reduced malondialdehyde and improved PSQI, while triglycerides, total and LDL cholesterol and CRP were null; very high heterogeneity for several outcomes limits certainty.

Randomized blinded three-arm study in 72 children with anxiety disorders and insomnia found both melatonin and clonidine improved sleep-habit scores versus placebo with no significant difference between active treatments; pediatric psychiatric context and short follow-up remain explicit.

Four-week randomized placebo-controlled trial in 80 adults with mild-to-moderate atopic dermatitis found melatonin improved SCORAD, pruritus, sleep and quality-of-life measures but not pain; short duration and disease-specific context limit broader claims.

Small randomized trial in 46 climacteric female nurses working fixed shifts found low-dose melatonin reduced symptom scores and improved reported sleep quality on days off without changing total sleep duration or reproductive hormones; sample size and shift-specific timing matter.

Six-week study in 40 adults receiving fluoxetine reported greater HDRS improvement with adjunctive magnesium than fluoxetine alone, while serum serotonin did not change; adjunctive design, small sample and allocation method prevent magnesium-monotherapy attribution.

Six-week randomized dietary trial in 50 women receiving breast-cancer chemotherapy found a tryptophan-rich meal plan increased actigraphic total sleep time at selected weeks and reduced WASO at selected weeks, without deep-sleep or fatigue benefit; food-pattern intervention cannot be treated as isolated tryptophan-supplement evidence.

Four-condition crossover trial in 14 trained men found nocturnal melatonin did not improve measured sleep, while morning caffeine drove shuttle-run performance benefits; combination biomarker changes cannot establish an independent melatonin performance effect.

Updated 24-RCT dose-response meta-analysis found melatoninergic agonists reduced ICU delirium incidence, with a similar signal in the melatonin subgroup, but mortality and adverse-event rates were unchanged; pooled duration and dose modeling is research context and must not be converted into dosing guidance.

Eight-week randomized double-blind trial in 85 healthy children with parent-reported attention, concentration or memory concerns found standardized ashwagandha root extract improved selected computerized cognitive outcomes and parent-reported sleep, with no significant adverse-event signal; pediatric findings and multiple secondary endpoints require cautious interpretation.

Single-blind randomized placebo-controlled study in 83 regular tobacco users reported lower tobacco-use frequency, dependence and craving after six months of alpha-linolenic-acid supplementation; cessation-clinic context, self-reported tobacco outcomes and the specific ALA formulation limit general omega-3 attribution.

Open-label eight-week pilot of adjunctive curcumin in only six youths with treatment-resistant bipolar depression reported improvement in global depression and illness severity with exploratory inflammatory and oxidative-stress biomarker analyses; absence of a control group makes efficacy highly preliminary.

Randomized trial in 240 men with mild-to-moderate depression found a probiotic product added to escitalopram produced larger improvements in depression scores and sexual-function domains than escitalopram alone; absence of a matched placebo, single-clinic population and adjunctive design prevent probiotic-monotherapy attribution.

Twelve-week randomized placebo-controlled trial in 60 healthy overweight or obese adults found strain-specific L. plantarum KABP051 effects on body weight, waist circumference and microbiome composition, with post-hoc signals for fatigue and confusion; mood findings were secondary and strain-specific.

Mendelian-randomization meta-analysis linked genetically predicted omega-3, omega-6 and their ratio with several psychiatric outcomes, but these genetic-instrument associations are not supplementation trials and should not be converted into treatment-effect or dosing claims.

Eight-week randomized double-blind trial in 75 healthy older adults found Pediococcus acidilactici PA53 improved happiness, gastrointestinal symptoms and PSQI with inflammatory-marker and microbiome changes; stress change was not significant within group, and effects remain specific to this strain and population.

Small randomized crossover trial in 28 healthy adults found a single dose of heat-treated L. gasseri CP2305 altered EEG alpha power, HRV and self-reported stress/tension versus placebo; acute postbiotic findings are formulation-specific and do not establish durable clinical anxiolytic benefit.

Pilot multicentre double-blind trial in 58 adults age 60 and older with moderate depression found modest overall symptom advantages from adjunct L. helveticus plus B. longum, but no significant group-by-time interaction, no added quality-of-life benefit and greater than 50% attrition over 24 weeks.

ProBioHRV randomized sub-study in 53 participants found no consistent probiotic effect on nutrient intake, dietary variety or diversity, with only exploratory diagnosis- and time-dependent signals; useful null counterweight to claims that probiotics broadly improve eating patterns through the gut-brain axis.

Eight-week 2x2 factorial RCT in 56 adults with obesity found no probiotic-by-fiber interaction, selective fiber effects on HDL and mood, weak probiotic metabolic effects after multiplicity correction, and no supported between-group sleep benefit; combined supplementation offered no added advantage.

Six-week randomized adjunctive study in 40 adults receiving fluoxetine found larger MoCA gains with magnesium, particularly attention and memory, but no significant between-group change in serum BDNF; small sample and concomitant antidepressant therapy prevent magnesium-only cognitive attribution.

Four-arm randomized blinded feasibility trial in 91 chemotherapy patients found inhaled lavender, jojoba, orange or ginger aromatherapy acceptable and feasible with lower composite symptom severity overall, but it was not designed to establish ingredient-specific efficacy and needs confirmatory trials.

Twelve-week double-blind RCT in 70 adults with work-related stress and mild-to-moderate insomnia found the Cerebiome probiotic did not outperform placebo on the primary insomnia outcome, although depressive symptoms showed a modest between-group signal; formulation-specific mood evidence remains secondary.

Systematic review of 13 clinical trials involving 785 people with multiple sclerosis found some nanocurcumin disability signals while EGCG, silymarin, cranberry and other curcumin formulations were largely null on disability, relapse or MRI outcomes; heterogeneity prevented meta-analysis and category transfer.

Systematic review of 21 human reports found antioxidant and inflammatory signals for turmeric or curcumin in hemodialysis but no consistent lipid-lowering effect; importantly, high-dose turmeric was associated with a food-drug interaction and nephrotoxicity in immunosuppressant users, making interaction context explicit.

Umbrella review covering seven meta-analyses and about 11,600 randomized participants found population-specific reductions in CRP, TNF-alpha, IL-6 and oxidative-stress markers with vitamin D, alongside null findings in several overweight, obese and asthma populations; effects are not universal anti-inflammatory evidence.

Meta-analysis of 30 case-control studies found lower plasma selenium, nail selenium and plasma zinc in women with breast cancer than controls, but all included evidence was observational with substantial heterogeneity and residual-confounding risk; this cannot establish prevention or supplementation benefit.

Double-blind crossover trial in 14 healthy adults found two weeks of a sulforaphane-precursor supplement did not improve endurance capacity but attenuated selected post-exercise CK and myoglobin responses and relative oxidative-stress changes; tiny sample and surrogate outcomes limit performance claims.

Ten-week RCT in 59 adults with excess weight found favorable within-group lipid and uric-acid changes when green-tea kombucha accompanied an energy-restricted diet, but between-group changes were not significant for evaluated markers; diet co-intervention prevents independent kombucha efficacy claims.

Multicentre phase-IV trial in 151 patients with painful diabetic neuropathy found pregabalin monotherapy non-inferior to pregabalin plus alpha-lipoic acid for pain reduction overall, with exploratory subgroup differences; combination results do not establish routine added benefit from alpha-lipoic acid.

Nine-day RCT in 24 healthy adults found a calcium-fructoborate, turmeric and pomegranate blend improved selected perceived pain, recovery and sleep outcomes after muscle-damaging exercise but not neuromuscular, inflammatory, oxidative-stress or muscle-damage biomarkers; ingredient-specific attribution is impossible.

Meta-analysis of seven randomized trials found green tea modestly lowered total cholesterol in postmenopausal women but did not significantly improve other prespecified metabolic outcomes; evidence quality was low and concentrated-extract hepatic-safety concerns warrant formulation caution.

Eight-week randomized trial in overweight or obese adults tested L-BAIBA alone and with grains of paradise alongside calorie restriction and exercise; the multicomponent lifestyle context and largely null group-by-time effects require separation of exploratory perceptual/metabolic findings from product efficacy claims.

Network meta-analysis of 28 RCTs and 3,650 heart-failure patients compared 15 distinct plant extracts and generated outcome-specific SUCRA rankings, but sparse direct comparisons and major formulation heterogeneity mean rankings cannot establish a single best botanical or justify cross-extract transfer.

Systematic review of 37 studies involving 1,597 mostly young participants found energy-drink exposure frequently increased heart rate and blood pressure and was associated with QTc and other ECG changes; multi-ingredient products and heterogeneous protocols prevent caffeine-only attribution.

Systematic review of 17 rodent studies found caffeine often reduced stress-related behavioral, oxidative and neuroinflammatory changes, but dose, route and model heterogeneity were substantial and animal findings cannot establish antidepressant or anxiolytic efficacy in humans.

Randomized crossover study in 16 recreational male tennis players found caffeine mouth rinsing improved selected groundstroke, volley and total targeting scores versus placebo/no-rinse control; tiny sport-specific study does not establish general cognitive enhancement.

Twelve-week randomized placebo-controlled trial in healthy children age 8 to 12 found no primary or secondary cognitive, mood or sleep benefit from sunflower phosphatidylserine in the full cohort; a predefined low-performing subgroup showed a visuospatial-memory signal only.

Twenty-eight-day randomized trial found a caffeine-based energy drink acutely increased energy expenditure and produced selected reaction-time, focus and energy effects, but the beverage matrix and repeated-exposure design prevent clean caffeine-versus-other-ingredient attribution.

Meta-analysis of only three RCTs and 358 dementia patients found choline alphoscerate favored citicoline on a geriatric clinical-assessment scale and several subdomains, while memory and word-fluency differences were null; the very small evidence base limits comparative claims.

Small randomized crossover trial in 14 physically active men tested a one-week creatine loading phase across sleep, cognition, physical performance and recovery; findings are acute-loading and male-athlete specific, so they should not be generalized to chronic cognitive use.

Pilot crossover study in 20 postmenopausal women found oral choline altered working-memory-related brain activation and connectivity without improving task performance; neuroimaging changes alone do not establish cognitive benefit.

Secondary analysis of a 12-week randomized trial in 32 healthy middle-aged and older adults found within-group TMAO elevation at the highest egg-phosphatidylcholine intake but no significant between-group difference versus placebo; values remained below high-risk thresholds.

Randomized crossover study in recreationally active men found morning caffeine improved selected strength-related measures, while cognitive outcomes varied by test; a single standardized morning protocol does not imply uniform cognitive enhancement.

Six-arm 16-week RCT in 103 older adults found high-load resistance training improved multiple physical and biomarker outcomes and creatine supplied some additional benefits, but the exercise-by-supplement factorial context prevents assigning all gains to creatine alone.

Systematic review/meta-analysis of nine studies and more than 7,000 assessments associated neonatal caffeine treatment with better motor and cognitive outcomes and lower cerebral-palsy odds but no clear language benefit; this is a neonatal medical-treatment context, not consumer stimulant evidence.

Randomized crossover study in 19 habitual caffeine users found higher theacrine exposures increased salivary cortisol without clear heart-rate, blood-pressure or cognitive benefit; this provides a useful stress-response and null-efficacy counterweight to stimulant marketing.

Randomized open-label comparison in 56 children with ADHD found phosphatidylserine did not significantly improve core ADHD symptoms, while atomoxetine did; phosphatidylserine showed some internalizing/externalizing behavior changes, but open-label active-comparator design limits inference.

Broad 2026 Ginkgo biloba review integrates extraction, delivery, mechanistic, clinical and toxicology literature; useful as a map of formulation and safety issues, but mixed evidence types and technologies should not be treated as a single efficacy estimate.

Systematic review spanning 42 preclinical studies and 23 clinical trials found possible cognitive and functional signals for Ginkgo after traumatic brain injury, while highlighting reported bleeding events especially with anticoagulants or NSAIDs; clinical certainty remains limited.

Systematic review/meta-analysis of 11 studies and 1,406 adults with schizophrenia found no significant overall symptom effect from caffeine, with mixed signals for negative symptoms, cognition and possible positive-symptom worsening; medication interactions and heterogeneity matter.

Randomized crossover trial in 16 male special-forces soldiers found caffeinated gum improved selected reaction-time, strength, jump, shooting and close-quarters-battle measures versus placebo; small elite-military sample sharply limits generalization.

Three-arm crossover trial in 15 professional male esports athletes found caffeine plus L-theanine and caffeine plus diaphragmatic breathing improved auditory reaction time and Aim Lab performance versus caffeine alone; ingredient-specific attribution is impossible for the combined arms.

Meta-analysis found caffeine increased P300 amplitude at moderate studied exposures but did not significantly change P300 latency, with high between-study heterogeneity; electrophysiological changes should remain separate from claims of meaningful cognitive improvement.

Small randomized crossover study in 12 college athletes found a multi-ingredient energy drink improved repeated-sprint output and attenuated aspects of cognitive fatigue versus placebo, but caffeine, anserine, elderberry and micronutrients were co-administered.

Three-level meta-analysis of 26 randomized crossover trials in female team-sport athletes found small favorable physical-performance effects from acute caffeine, while sport-specific and cognitive estimates were less certain; domain-specific effects and evidence certainty should remain explicit.

Prospective cohort plus dose-response meta-analysis found a nonlinear association between dietary choline and incident dementia, with moderate—not highest—intakes associated with lower risk in some analyses; observational nutrition data cannot establish supplementation benefit.

Randomized double-masked study in 116 adults found both an energy drink and caffeine-matched control improved sustained attention and alertness similarly, with no strength or static-endurance advantage from the energy drink; results point to caffeine rather than proprietary extras.

Large crossover study of 51 recreationally active men found morning caffeine did not significantly improve the tested cognitive battery or reactive-agility outcomes versus placebo/no-pill control, providing a useful direct null against blanket morning-performance claims.

Ten-week double-blind RCT in 100 older adults found no overall MoCA advantage from beta-alanine, although participants with below-normal baseline cognition showed subgroup improvement; mood and physical-function outcomes were largely null.

Systematic review of seven combat-sport clinical trials reported some improvements in strength, power, work capacity and sport-specific measures with beta-alanine, but the small heterogeneous evidence base and mixed perceptual/biochemical findings limit broad performance claims.

Small mechanistic trial in only 10 analyzed older adults with lower baseline cognition found beta-alanine increased fractional anisotropy in the hippocampus and amygdala without changing BDNF or inflammatory markers; MRI changes are hypothesis-generating, not clinical proof.

Four-week RCT in 27 high-intensity functional-training participants found beta-alanine improved vertical-jump and jumping-power measures but did not clearly alter fatigue, exercise metabolic intensity or perceived intensity.

Triple-blind crossover study in 21 resistance-trained men found caffeine, beta-alanine and their combination produced little consistent mechanical advantage during upper-body superset training; beta-alanine alone reduced last-repetition velocity versus placebo on one measure.

Bayesian network meta-analysis of 67 RCTs involving 1,026 elite combat-sport athletes compared 26 supplements; rankings varied by outcome and discipline, so indirect SUCRA-style hierarchy should not be translated into a universal best supplement.

Network meta-analysis of swimming interventions found outcome-specific signals for L-arginine, beta-alanine and creatine plus sodium bicarbonate, while several swimming-time outcomes were null; indirect comparisons and sparse networks constrain rankings.

Three-month randomized feasibility trial in 27 adults with overweight or obesity found sustained-release beta-alanine was tolerated and adhered to, but showed low probability of meaningful cardiometabolic, cardiovascular or routine biochemical effects.

Fourteen-week beta-alanine plus HIIT study in 13 active men found no improvement in serum BDNF or Stroop performance; training improved selected cardiorespiratory outcomes independently, providing direct null cognitive evidence.

Post-hoc randomized-trial analysis found carnosine improved selected cognition speed and efficiency outcomes mainly in the youngest adult age stratum; subgroup/post-hoc status means the finding needs prospective confirmation.

Four-week six-arm basketball trial found sprint-interval training improved performance across groups and supplement arms showed larger changes than placebo on selected outcomes, but small groups and combined creatine/beta-alanine/citrulline conditions complicate ingredient attribution.

Four-week randomized trial in competitive adolescent middle- and long-distance runners found beta-alanine improved time to exhaustion but not aerobic capacity, reinforcing that endurance-test effects do not equal VO2max improvement.

Two-week high-dose beta-alanine RCT in 16 trained futsal players found no significant supplementation-by-time benefit for intermittent endurance, 30-m sprint, lactate or perceived exertion despite overall training/time improvements.

Systematic review of nine studies in trained participants suggested beta-alanine strength/power findings may vary with exposure pattern and training metabolic demand, but this literature synthesis is heterogeneous and studied protocols must not become dosing recommendations.

Triple-blind crossover trial in 17 recreational male runners found an acute betalain-rich concentrate did not improve running economy or VO2max, although heart rate, perceived exertion and post-exercise muscle oxygenation showed selected favorable changes.

Four-condition crossover trial in 13 resistance-trained men found caffeine improved several squat strength/power measures while beetroot juice and combination conditions affected selected endurance outcomes; no uniform additive synergy was established.

Small crossover trial in 12 resistance-trained men reported selected strength, fatigue and recovery benefits after short-term beetroot-juice supplementation, but sample size and multiple endpoints make the magnitude and reproducibility uncertain.

Umbrella review of 15 meta-analyses found statistically significant but generally negligible-to-small beetroot-juice effects on strength, VO2max and time-to-exhaustion; effect size and population differences argue against broad performance promises.

Triple-blind crossover study in 20 young men found caffeine, with or without beta-alanine, acutely raised intraocular pressure at rest while beta-alanine alone did not; exercise subsequently reduced ocular-pressure measures regardless of supplement.

Meta-analysis of eight RCTs and 377 participants with prediabetes or type 2 diabetes found carnosine/beta-alanine interventions reduced fasting glucose and HbA1c but not several lipid, insulin or anthropometric outcomes; interventions and populations were heterogeneous.

Randomized double-blind trial in 68 highly trained female basketball players found sodium-bicarbonate-containing arms improved initial Wingate peak power, whereas beta-alanine alone did not improve measured physical-capacity outcomes; combination effects require separation.

Four-week double-blind RCT in 28 trained male kickboxers found beta-alanine improved total kickboxing anaerobic work and push-up/pull-up endurance but not jump power, best effort or performance-decrement index.

Crossover study in 12 young men found beetroot juice prevented an early post-resistance-exercise reduction in flow-mediated dilation without clear differences in blood pressure or several hemodynamic measures; this is an acute vascular surrogate finding.

Twelve-week double-blind RCT in 64 sedentary adults age 70 and older found oral nitrite did not improve skeletal-muscle mitochondrial respiration, exercise capacity or physical function despite acute platelet bioenergetic effects.

Systematic review of water-polo ergonutrition described possible roles for whey protein, beta-alanine, L-arginine, spirulina and other supplements, but the sport-specific evidence base is sparse and heterogeneous and should remain category-level context.

Twelve-week double-blind RCT in 120 people with or at risk for metabolic syndrome found ginger, cinnamon and black-seed interventions improved selected glucose and lipid markers versus placebo, but the parallel spice arms should not be collapsed into a single ingredient effect.

Systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized trials evaluated garlic across glycemic and lipid outcomes; formulation, duration and population heterogeneity mean pooled biomarker effects should remain separate from cardiovascular-event claims.

Randomized placebo-controlled ENDOTALLIUM study tested encapsulated purple-garlic oil on microvascular function and metabolic-syndrome components; product-specific vascular and metabolic findings should not be generalized to all garlic preparations.

Systematic review/meta-analysis of randomized trials found cinnamon associated with changes in selected metabolic biomarkers in type 2 diabetes, but substantial variation in species, preparations, exposures and baseline treatment limits product-level certainty.

Eight-week double-blind RCT in adults at risk for hypertension found freeze-dried garlic extract lowered systolic, diastolic and mean arterial pressure and improved several lipid markers versus placebo while increasing nitric-oxide levels.

Twelve-week double-blind RCT in 70 people with MAFLD found berberine improved ALT, de Ritis ratio and total-cholesterol change, while most other glucose and lipid outcomes were not significantly different from placebo.

Randomized comparative study in 50 adults with obesity found berberine and Gymnema sylvestre produced different body-composition, glucose, blood-pressure and adipokine-expression changes; active-comparator design does not establish superiority against placebo.

Meta-analysis of 21 RCTs in dyslipidemia reported reductions in total cholesterol, triglycerides and LDL with a small HDL increase from garlic, but product forms and study quality vary across the pooled evidence.

Eight-week double-blind RCT in mildly hypercholesterolemic adults found a standardized onion-plus-garlic extract lowered LDL and total cholesterol with selected blood-pressure and inflammatory changes; the combined formulation prevents garlic-only attribution.

Umbrella review of cinnamon meta-analyses found small average reductions in systolic and diastolic pressure and selected antioxidant/IL-6 signals, while CRP, MDA and ICAM-1 were not consistently improved.

Randomized double-blind controlled trial evaluated Ceylon-cinnamon extract on glucose, lipids and safety in adults; species-specific extract evidence should not be transferred to cassia cinnamon or culinary cinnamon generally.

Twelve-week randomized double-blind trial found combined berberine plus cinnamon lowered fasting glucose, HbA1c and selected lipid measures versus placebo in type 2 diabetes; the combination design cannot identify the contribution of either ingredient.

Phase-2 randomized trial of berberine ursodeoxycholate in inadequately controlled type 2 diabetes assessed glycemic, hepatic and cardiometabolic outcomes; this is a distinct pharmaceutical conjugate and must not be treated as ordinary berberine-supplement evidence.

Bayesian network meta-analysis compared curcumin, resveratrol, silymarin and berberine for cardiometabolic risk markers in type 2 diabetes; indirect rankings across heterogeneous products and trials are category evidence, not a universal botanical hierarchy.

Mixed clinical/preclinical meta-analysis found berberine lowered fasting glucose in the small clinical evidence base and showed broader biochemical effects in animal models; the 4-clinical-trial subset is too limited to inherit the stronger preclinical signals.

Umbrella review of 21 meta-analyses reported cinnamon-associated improvements in fasting glucose and lipid profiles in metabolic disease, but methodological quality, overlapping trials and formulation heterogeneity temper certainty.

Double-blind RCT in 70 overweight or obese adults with MAFLD examined berberine effects on VEGF, arterial stiffness and vascular measures; vascular-surrogate findings should remain distinct from demonstrated clinical cardiovascular benefit.

Meta-analysis of 10 RCTs found adjunctive garlic lowered blood pressure in hypertension, while effect sizes varied by formulation, duration and population; findings support a biomarker-level signal rather than replacement of antihypertensive therapy.

Randomized double-blind placebo-controlled trial evaluated Ceylon cinnamon in diabetes; the receipt remains species- and preparation-specific and should not be merged with cassia-cinnamon evidence without formulation verification.

Large multicenter six-month RCT in 337 diabetes-free adults with obesity and MASLD found berberine did not significantly reduce visceral-adipose area or liver-fat content versus placebo, providing a high-value null against weight/fat-loss claims.

Four-week randomized crossover trial in healthy adults and adults with metabolic syndrome found decaffeinated green-tea extract reduced circulating endotoxin and selected gut-inflammatory/permeability markers and fasting glucose, without a systemic-inflammatory effect.

Ten-week RCT found green-tea kombucha added to caloric restriction did not enhance weight or fat loss versus caloric restriction alone, although selected inflammation, lipid-accumulation and salivary-microbiome measures differed.

Large systematic review/meta-analysis of 281 studies found different polyphenol classes produced modest outcome-specific changes in blood pressure, lipids and glycemic markers; pooling across catechins, anthocyanins, curcumin and others requires a category firewall.

Meta-analysis of 15 trials and 722 participants with type 2 diabetes reported improvements in fasting glucose, HbA1c and insulin-resistance indices with green tea, but product composition and trial heterogeneity remain important.

Meta-analysis of 145 RCTs and 5,205 participants found flavan-3-ol-rich foods/supplements modestly reduced office and ambulatory blood pressure, with larger effects at higher baseline pressure; interventions spanned cocoa, tea, grape, apple and isolated compounds.

Four-week randomized double-blind trial in 50 older or metabolically at-risk adults found quercetin glycoside preconditioning did not improve SARS-CoV-2 booster neutralizing antibodies, spike-specific IgG, or CD4/CD8 T-cell responses versus placebo; useful direct null immune evidence.

Systematic review of nine RCTs and 503 head-and-neck-cancer patients found turmeric/curcumin preparations showed potential for prevention or treatment of therapy-related oral mucositis, but routes included oral products, mouthwashes and gels and certainty varied.

Three-week triple-blind pilot RCT in 64 hypertensive adults found a compound fish-oil product improved selected coronary Doppler velocities but not blood pressure, skin or brain microcirculation; omega-3, resveratrol, astaxanthin and CoQ10 were co-formulated.

Broad review maps curcumin evidence across endothelial function, lipid metabolism, inflammation and neuroprotection, but mixes mechanistic and clinical literature and therefore cannot supply a single quantitative efficacy estimate.

Eight-week randomized double-blind trial in 60 migraine patients found a curcumin-gingerol-piperine blend reduced hs-CRP, nitric oxide and headache severity but not headache frequency or duration; multicomponent formulation prevents curcumin-only attribution.

GRADE-based meta-analysis found curcumin reduced severe radiation-injury incidence and severity/pain scores but not overall radiation-injury incidence; heterogeneous oncology settings and formulations limit generalization.

Systematic review of curcumin in MASLD highlights anti-inflammatory, oxidative, metabolic and mitochondrial mechanisms alongside clinical evidence, while explicitly flagging low bioavailability, combination-therapy complexity and lack of standardized protocols.

Comprehensive turmeric review integrates botany, traditional use, phytochemistry, pharmacokinetics and clinical literature; low bioavailability and limited therapeutic efficacy remain major translational constraints despite extensive mechanistic evidence.

Systematic review found resveratrol evidence for glycemic, inflammatory, oxidative and pancreatic effects is driven heavily by experimental and type-2-diabetes literature, with direct evidence for pancreatogenic diabetes remaining scarce.

Umbrella meta-analysis found curcumin did not significantly improve BMI or waist circumference in MAFLD and produced only a small weight reduction; evidence strength for anthropometric benefit was low to moderate.

Pilot randomized double-blind trial in 82 preschool children with recurrent wheezing found a resveratrol plus beta-glucan nasal spray was safe but missed its primary respiratory-symptom endpoint; secondary trends favoring the product were not statistically definitive.

Six-month multicenter pilot RCT in 40 children with asthma and allergic rhinitis found a multicomponent postbiotic/immunonutrition product improved prespecified symptom-control measures versus placebo; seven active components prevent single-ingredient attribution.

Systematic review found zero eligible phenotype-defined RCTs testing isolated vitamin D or resveratrol in adults with rigorously defined sarcopenic obesity, documenting a genuine evidence gap despite strong mechanistic rationale.

Meta-analysis of six comparative studies and 697 men with BPH found adjunct curcumin improved symptom scores and selected urinary/prostate measures, but substantial heterogeneity and concomitant alpha-blocker/5-alpha-reductase-inhibitor use constrain independent-effect claims.

Systematic review of 105 studies found outcome-specific metabolic signals for anthocyanins, curcumin and resveratrol, with resveratrol results especially inconsistent; evidence should stay compound-specific rather than pooled as generic antioxidant efficacy.

Twelve-week double-blind ATLAS RCT in 84 adults with knee osteoarthritis found a Boswellia/pine-bark/MSM/curcumin/piperine combination produced no pain benefit over placebo and had a similar adverse-event profile.

Systematic review of 16 preclinical and six clinical studies found resveratrol consistently improved periodontal outcomes in animals but clinical trials were small, heterogeneous and short, with no clinical study assessing radiographic bone loss.
Randomized clinical evidence examined systemic resveratrol as an adjunct to periodontal treatment in smokers; this receipt remains indication- and co-treatment-specific pending broader replication.

Systematic review/meta-analysis evaluated adjunct resveratrol for periodontal disease; pooled periodontal findings should remain adjunctive-treatment evidence rather than proof of general systemic anti-inflammatory benefit.

Systematic review of 13 mechanistic and human studies found quercetin showed anti-inflammatory and immunomodulatory signals across autoimmune conditions, but few clinical trials and heterogeneous diseases/designs prevent broad therapeutic conclusions.

Systematic review/meta-analysis evaluated microbiota-modulating interventions in pediatric type 1 diabetes; diverse probiotic, prebiotic and synbiotic strategies require category-level interpretation rather than strain-independent efficacy claims.

Randomized four-arm phase-II trial in Kenyan infants tested pro/synbiotic strategies for systemic inflammation and gut health; population, formulation and early-life context must remain explicit when interpreting immune effects.

Meta-analysis of 14 RCTs and 1,739 children found probiotics improved nasal/eye symptoms and quality of life in allergic rhinitis, but heterogeneity exceeded 90% for major clinical outcomes, limiting strain-independent conclusions.

Eight-week randomized placebo-controlled COPD trial found a multistrain probiotic reduced IL-6 and improved CAT scores, while between-group spirometric differences were not significant and IL-17/TGF-beta were unchanged.

Exploratory randomized double-blind placebo-controlled trial evaluated VSL#3 for abdominal pain and bloating in ulcerative-colitis remission with IBS-like symptoms; findings remain product- and phenotype-specific.
